subject.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)

question: Should runtime registry loading invalidate legacy no-pluginId/no-code diagnostics with missing absolute sources, or should that cleanup live only in doctor/migration-owned repair code?
rationale: The explicit marker follows prior maintainer direction, but the legacy branch intentionally changes upgraded persisted-state behavior inside runtime registry loading, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Accept Runtime Invalidation With Proof
options.body: Require redacted latest-head live output or logs for the legacy no-code SQLite row, then land the runtime invalidation as a bounded upgrade repair.

options.title: Accept Source And Test Proof
options.body: Maintainers can waive external proof and accept the current source/tests as enough for this small persisted-state compatibility change.

options.title: Move Legacy Cleanup To Doctor
options.body: Pause or revise the PR so runtime only handles explicit markers and legacy no-code cleanup is performed by doctor or migration code.

recommendation.title: Accept Runtime Invalidation With Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted latest-head live output or logs for the legacy no-code SQLite row, then land the runtime invalidation as a bounded upgrade repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the merged stale diagnostic registry fix and SQLite plugin index history this PR changes.
